text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites, and articles. Users can guide an LLM by writing clear instructions, which is called prompt engineering. LLMs are good at tasks like answering questions, summarising texts, and writing emails. However, they also have limits. They sometimes give wrong information, cannot think like humans, and may reflect biases found in their training data. So it is wise to check their answers carefully.
